title: Spark Execution Basics
learningOutcome: Trace Spark execution from SparkSession + config through lazy transforms to the action that creates Jobs, Stages, Tasks, and Executors
description: Understanding Spark Internals · Episode 1. Read a frozen exhibit that builds SparkSession with executor cores/memory, applies lazy transformations, then an action. Answer questions in that same order. History Server confirms the Job. Pass ≥ 80%.

problemStatement.overview: Using a frozen History Server application for a narrow-only Acme pipeline, explain Spark jobs, stages, tasks, executors, and lazy evaluation.
symptoms: Learners can write DataFrame code but cannot read what Spark actually ran.
Extra mid-pipeline actions (count/show) are misunderstood as free.
yourTaskSteps: Open the frozen submission’s History Server application page.
Inspect Jobs, Stages, Tasks, and Executors for this exhibit.
Answer the graded questions in questions.json (terminology + exhibit facts).
Score at least 80% (8 of 10) to pass.
problemStatement.yourTask: Pass the Spark Execution Basics quiz from the frozen History Server exhibit.
hints: filter and withColumn are transformations; write is an action.
One action usually creates one Job on the Jobs tab.
Task count tracks partitions; executor count is the worker pool size.
